question: Once the war comes to an end, some Ukrainian soldiers returning from the front will make their way to Poland. As early as February, the Chief Commissioner of the Polish Police, Inspector General Marek Boroń, warned that some may be suffering from mental health issues, and that their combat experience and weapons from the front line could be exploited by criminal groups1.

Ukrainian citizens holding biometric passports benefit from visa-free travel. Meanwhile, those covered by temporary protection may legally reside in the EU and travel to other Schengen countries. This protection has been extended until 4 March 2028. The suspension of visa-free travel will therefore not resolve the issue of veterans who are already within the Schengen area2. 1.
Will the Commission introduce a ban on entry to the Schengen area for veterans of the Ukrainian armed forces?
Will the Commission restrict the freedom of movement within the Schengen area for Ukrainian veterans who are already present within its territory, including those under temporary protection?
